kjv: Saul reigned one year; and when he had reigned two years over Israel,
mine: Saul was [number missing] years old when he became king, and he reigned two years over Israel.
note: Hebrew ben-shanah Sha'ul be-malkho is the standard regnal formula "Saul was X years old when he became king" (cf. 2 Sam 2:10), with the number lost in transmission; the KJV reinterprets "son of a year" as length of reign and runs the verse into v. 2.

kjv: in high places, and in pits
note: Hebrew tseriach is a cellar, crypt or tomb-chamber (some suggest a stronghold), not an elevated cult site; bor is a cistern.
MT reads Geva', a town distinct from Gibeah (Giv'ah) though close by; the KJV conforms it to Gibeah of v. 15.

kjv: Yet they (the Israelites) had a file for the mattocks
mine: The charge was a pim for the plowshares and the mattocks
note: Hebrew pim was unknown in 1611; inscribed weights found in excavations show it is a weight of about two-thirds of a shekel, so the verse states the Philistines' fee for sharpening tools, not that Israel had files.
